messages.author: c027a0d4ee83ac1a
messages.subject: QTL scan
parts:
Hi Karl & R/QTL friends,
Please I want to find out if the pheno data for R/QTL is restricted to 1.
I have five phenotype data in my first 5 columns and I want to run scanone but I am unsure as to how to write pheno.col = 
 I tried both codes below but didn't work and would be glad if anyone here can help

mydata.scan1<- scanone(mydata_reduced,pheno.col = 1:5, method = "em")
                                     and
mydata.scan1<- scanone(mydata_reduced,pheno.col = "PH","SD","DTF","Biomass","brix", method = "em")

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: QTL scan
parts:
scanone() can do genome scans on multiple phenotypes; it will do a genome scan on each phenotype individually and the output will be a data frame with chromosome, position, and then a set of LOD score columns.  See page 5 of the "shorter tour of R/qtl", https://rqtl.org/tutorials/rqtltour2.pdf

When you say "it didn't work", can you give more details, particularly the exact error message.

In the first instance, pheno.col=1:5 should be valid, provided that you have at least 5 phenotypes.

In the second instance, you need to combine the multiple phenotype names into a vector using c().

    mydata.scan1<- scanone(mydata_reduced,pheno.col = c("PH","SD","DTF","Biomass","brix"), method = "em")

karl

parts:
These are warning messages rather than error messages, meaning that you are still getting output but you maybe should check that it looks okay.

The “X’X matrix is singular” means that a linear regression was over-specified and could not be fit. But it may be that this is happening at a few positions and only in some permutation replicates, and so the warnings might be ignorable.

karl

On Wed, May 27, 2020 at 7:17 PM Karl Broman <kbr...@gmail.com> wrote:
scanone() can do genome scans on multiple phenotypes; it will do a genome scan on each phenotype individually and the output will be a data frame with chromosome, position, and then a set of LOD score columns.  See page 5 of the "shorter tour of R/qtl", https://rqtl.org/tutorials/rqtltour2.pdf

When you say "it didn't work", can you give more details, particularly the exact error message.

In the first instance, pheno.col=1:5 should be valid, provided that you have at least 5 phenotypes.

In the second instance, you need to combine the multiple phenotype names into a vector using c().

    mydata.scan1<- scanone(mydata_reduced,pheno.col = c("PH","SD","DTF","Biomass","brix"), method = "em")

karl
